message.content: Lions mate during the breeding season (typically spring and summer). A male will approach a receptive female, often after establishing dominance over other males. He may scent-mark or roar to attract her. Once she signals readiness—usually by standing with her tail up—the male mounts her from behind. Copulation lasts only a few minutes, but females can mate with multiple males, leading to paternity confusion and increased offspring survival. After mating, the male may guard the female and later help protect the cubs.
